openPoints: If production source maps are deployed with the application, how is the claim that the production artifact excludes the bridge reconciled with those maps still containing __og_e2e and the mutation command source text?
What release-pipeline control prevents an explicit --mode e2e artifact, which is otherwise a valid optimized Vite build, from being promoted to a production environment by mistake?

Which browser-level standard-profile test demonstrates that query parameters, local storage, and ordinary runtime interaction cannot create the bridge, rather than inferring that property only from emitted JavaScript marker scans?
How will CI detect contract drift when an existing Playwright scenario starts using a new bridge command that is absent from the installer contract or production-exclusion marker list?
architectureTip: Treat the E2E build as a separately classified artifact with release-policy enforcement, and validate both executable bundles and deployable metadata at the profile boundary.
topFinding: Compile-time mode replacement and tree shaking remove the executable bridge from standard JavaScript, but standard source maps still contain bridge identifiers and the build pipeline has no explicit guard against deploying the instrumented e2e profile.
